transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes — but because it’s happening during the drying cycle, treat it cautiously.

Stop using the dryer function and unplug the machine if the smell is burning, electrical, hot plastic/rubber, or if there’s any smoke, excessive heat, or unusual noise. Don’t leave it running unattended. A failed heater, fan, belt, or lint build-up inside can cause this and needs an engineer.

If the smell is more musty/damp, and drying performance has gradually got worse, these are the safe things to clean/check:

1. Clean the pump/drain filter
• Usually behind the small flap at the bottom front.
• Switch off/unplug first, put towels and a shallow tray down, then remove debris such as hair, coins and lint.
• Refit it securely. A restricted drain can affect drying.

2. Clean the door seal and inside of the door
• Wipe out trapped fluff, hair and detergent residue, especially in the folds of the rubber seal.
• Check the door glass and the area around the door opening too.

3. Clean the detergent drawer
• Remove it if possible and wash it with warm water.
• Clean the drawer housing, particularly the conditioner section, where mould and residue can build up.

4. Run a hot maintenance wash — without laundry
• Use a washing-machine cleaner, or follow the Hotpoint manual’s instructions.
• Run a 60–90°C cotton cycle. This helps remove detergent sludge that can smell when the machine heats up.

5. Check the water supply and drain hose
• Washer-dryers often use water during drying to condense moisture. Make sure the cold-water tap is fully open and hoses are not kinked.
• Make sure the drain hose is not squashed or blocked.

6. Don’t overload it for drying
• A washer-dryer generally dries a much smaller load than it can wash — often about half the wash capacity. Overloading leaves clothes damp and can make the machine run hot.

Unlike a separate tumble dryer, many Hotpoint washer-dryers do not have a user-accessible lint filter. Fluff can accumulate internally around the fan/heater, and that is not a job to dismantle yourself — especially where there is a smell.

### Arrange a repair rather than cleaning it further if:
• the smell is burning, acrid, or electrical;
• the dryer gets very hot but clothes remain damp;
• you hear scraping, thumping, or a fan not running;
• it trips the electrics;
• cleaning the filter and doing a maintenance wash does not fix it.

Have the model number ready (usually inside the door opening or on the back) and contact Hotpoint or a qualified appliance engineer. Also check Hotpoint’s official safety/recall checker for your exact model before using the drying function again.

It's more like burning dust or scorched fabric than musty. The top of the machine feels very hot during drying, and once I thought I saw a faint haze near the door seal. I've still been using it though. What should I do?

Stop using it immediately — including the washing function until it has been checked. Unplug it from the wall (don’t just switch it off), and do not run another drying cycle to “test” it.

A very hot top can occur to some extent during drying, but burning/scorched smells plus visible haze near the door seal are not normal and could indicate overheating of the heater, fan, wiring, belt, seals, or lint/fluff inside the machine.

What to do now:

• If it is currently hot, smoking, or smells strongly of burning: keep clear, ventilate the room if safe to do so, and call your local fire/emergency service if smoke continues or there is any sign of fire. Do not pour water on it or open panels.
• Once cool, leave it unplugged. If accessible without moving the machine, turn off the water supply too.
• Do not attempt an internal clean or remove covers. Washer-dryers can retain heat and have electrical components/heater ducts inside that need proper inspection.
• Arrange a repair with Hotpoint/Whirlpool or a qualified appliance engineer. Tell them specifically: “burning-dust/scorched-fabric smell during drying, machine becomes very hot on top, and faint haze/smoke seen by the door seal.” That should be treated as a safety-related fault, not a routine cleaning issue.
• Check the model and serial number label (commonly around the door opening, on the rear, or behind the detergent drawer) against any current Hotpoint/Whirlpool product-safety notices in your country before using it again.

If you can smell burning even when it is switched off, see melted plastic, or notice scorching around the plug/socket, keep it unplugged and have the socket and appliance checked urgently.
